Learn more about Accessibility How to Check Website Accessibility Read the blog Understanding Web Content Accessibility Guidlines Read the blog Digital Accessibility Made Simple Read the blog FAQs Check out the Accessibility FAQs if you’re short on time What is a Web Accessibility Tool? A web accessibility tool helps teams identify and fix barriers that prevent people with disabilities from using a website. Tools range from browser plugins and code validators to enterprise platforms like Glassbox, which monitors accessibility in real user sessions. Glassbox not only checks your site against WCAG and ADA standards but also shows how real users experience it, making compliance actionable. What is WCAG vs ADA? Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) are a global set of technical standards that define how to make digital content accessible. The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is U.S. legislation that requires equal access and is often enforced using WCAG as the benchmark. In short, WCAG sets the “how,” while ADA defines the “why” and carries legal weight for organizations operating in the U.S. How to Make a Website Accessible for the Visually Impaired? Start by ensuring that all visual content has accurate text alternatives, like alt text for images and labels for form fields. Use sufficient color contrast, scalable fonts and logical heading structures to make content readable with screen readers or magnifiers. Glassbox Accessibility helps by detecting these issues automatically in user sessions, so fixes can be prioritized and addressed quickly. How Do I Check if My Website is ADA Compliant? You can check ADA compliance by running automated scans, performing manual tests with screen readers and validating against WCAG success criteria. Glassbox provides real-time monitoring, session-based scoring and code-level guidance for ongoing compliance. This ensures your website stays aligned with ADA expectations and reduces the risk of lawsuits or accessibility gaps.

With tagless data capture, real-time insights and flexible deployment options, Glassbox empowers organizations to resolve digital friction, detect fraud and maintain compliance—all while delivering seamless user experiences. Take a self-guided tourGet a demo Enterprise-grade capabilities Data security & compliance Session fingerprinting Post-update session replays AI-powered privacy Data security: keeping PII private Glassbox protects Personally Identifiable Information (PII) with patented real-time masking technology for both mobile and desktop. Default masking enables businesses to capture complete user data while maintaining compliance with GDPR, CCPA and other data protection regulations. Glassbox simplifies the masking process by allowing non-developers to define rules directly within Session Replay. Multilayered identifiers ensure accurate masking, adapting to changes in app structures and avoiding overmasking that can obscure valuable insights. For complex use cases, Glassbox Professional Services provides expert remote assistance to keep your privacy measures precise and robust. Session fingerprinting: consistent data across domains Glassbox’s session fingerprinting technology ensures seamless stitching of cross-domain sessions, giving businesses a complete view of user journeys—even when users move between unauthenticated and authenticated spaces within a single session. For example, an online banking customer visiting the bank’s homepage might click "Login," redirecting to a login page on a different domain. Without session fingerprinting, this redirection would result in fragmented session data and higher abandonment rates from the homepage. Glassbox resolves this by capturing the entire journey as a single, unified session, enabling financial institutions and other regulated industries to gain actionable insights without the challenges of split sessions. Preserving historical session replays post-update Frequent code updates are a reality for website and app owners. While Glassbox’s tagless solution ensures uninterrupted data capture for new interactions, changes to code can sometimes cause previously recorded sessions to display incorrectly, with blank pages or missing elements. To address this, Glassbox provides advanced capabilities that ensure historical session data remains accurate and accessible, even after significant updates. Retroactive replays With Classet, Glassbox ensures retroactive session replays function flawlessly, even after significant code changes. Data integrity Glassbox preserves the integrity of session data, enabling businesses to compare performance across different code versions. Compliance Organizations can maintain compliance records without data disruptions, meeting regulatory and audit requirements. AI tools trusted by the most sensitive industries The Glassbox Insights Assistant (GIA) is powered by Microsoft’s OpenAI and is trusted by the largest banks in the United States for its robust security and cutting-edge capabilities. GIA ensures that sensitive data is handled with the highest levels of protection, meeting the stringent security requirements of regulated industries. GIA simplifies the analysis of digital interactions by enabling businesses to extract actionable insights effortlessly. From natural language queries locating specific sessions to concise summaries of sessions or reports, GIA helps teams resolve issues faster and make data-driven decisions with confidence. By combining advanced AI with enterprise-grade security, GIA sets a new standard for customer intelligence. Learn more Allow all cookies Cookie settings Glossary Digital analytics and customer experience glossary Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting in the field, this glossary will help you grasp the key elements that shape today's digital landscape. Dive in and expand your knowledge with clear and concise definitions, empowering you to make data-driven decisions and deliver exceptional user experiences. Skip to letter Skip to letter A B C D E F G H I K L M N O P Q R S T U V W a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z a A/B Testing A/B testing is a method of comparing two versions of a web page or app to determine which one performs better in terms of user engagement and conversion rates. Abandonment Rate The percentage of users who begin a process, such as filling out a form or making a purchase, but do not complete it, often indicating user frustration or inefficiencies in the user experience. Accessibility The degree to which a website or app can be used by people with disabilities. Acquisition Cost Acquisition cost, also known as Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), represents the cost of acquiring a new customer. App Attribution The process of determining where users come from before they download and install a mobile app, often used to track the effectiveness of marketing campaigns. App Crash Rate The percentage of times a mobile app crashes or fails to load on a user's device. App Crashes Instances where a mobile app unexpectedly shuts down or stops functioning properly. App Engagement Rate The level of interaction and activity that users have within a mobile app. App Install Attribution The process of attributing app installations or downloads to specific marketing campaigns or channels to measure the effectiveness of user acquisition efforts. App Performance Optimization The practice of analyzing and improving the performance, speed, and overall quality of a mobile app to enhance user experience, reduce crashes, and increase user satisfaction. App Retention The percentage of users who continue to use a mobile app over a given time period. App Retention Cohort A group of users who started using a mobile app during a specific period and are tracked to understand their retention patterns. App Session Length The duration of time that a user spends in a mobile app during a single session. App Session Replay The process of recording and reviewing a user's interactions within a mobile app. App Speed The amount of time it takes for a mobile app to load and become functional on a user's device. App Store Conversion Rate The percentage of users who download a mobile app after visiting its app store page. App Store Optimization (ASO) The process of optimizing mobile app metadata, keywords, and visual assets to improve app visibility and drive organic downloads and user engagement. App Store Reviews User-generated ratings and reviews of a mobile app on app store platforms. App Usage The number of times a mobile app is launched and the amount of time users spend within it. Application Performance Monitoring (APM) Application Performance Monitoring (APM) is a comprehensive approach to monitoring and managing the performance of software applications. It involves the use of specialized tools and techniques to collect data on various aspects of an application's performance, such as response times, resource utilization, error rates, and user satisfaction.
